ops.title: Graphite submit contract: gt posts ONE prs entry per call and loops — never re-batch the downstack
ops.body:
`POST /v1/graphite/submit/pull-requests` takes a `prs` array by schema, and gt never puts more than one element in it. This is the contract as recovered verbatim from the graphite-cli 1.7.20 bundle and confirmed against gt 1.8.6 through an HTTPS recorder (2026-09-02). It exists so nobody re-batches the stack into one call: 0.52.0 did, and every multi-branch submit came back `400 Bad Request` after every branch was already force-pushed.

## What was observed

| sender | prs entries | result |
|---|---|---|
| ccx | 1 (create) | 200, PR #17356 |
| gt | 1 each, x4 (creates, non-trunk bases) | 200, PRs #17357-#17360 |
| ccx | 5 (all create) | 400 |
| ccx | 2 (update + create) | 400 |

gt opened the same four branches off non-trunk bases with the same recorded `parent_branch_revision` ccx sends as `baseSha`, so no single branch or field is at fault. The batched array is the one property both failures share and no success has.

NOT proven: that the server rejects multi-entry arrays as such. The 400 body was never captured (the failing run predates 0.54.0's body quoting). The shape evidence above is the whole basis for the fix.

## gt's submit loop, verbatim (graphite-cli 1.7.20)

```
for(const n of p){const r=await D({submissionInfos:[n],mergeWhenReady:...,rerequestReview:...,comment:...,trunkBranchName:i,targetTrunkBranchName:f,openAfterSubmitting:...,gti:...,webSubmit:l,webSubmitAnalytics:h,context:t}); x===n.head&&(O=r)}
```

`submissionInfos:[n]`: one entry per POST, looped bottom-up.

## gt's order of operations for `gt submit --stack`

1. ONE batched `pull-request-info` for the whole stack; create-vs-update decided locally per branch from the cached prNumber.
2. Build all entries.
3. ONE batched `pre-submit-pull-requests` for the whole set. Its `retargetedPrs` response is awaited and ignored client-side; it is never read back into the entries.
4. ONE atomic multi-ref push for every branch, OUTSIDE the submit loop:
   `git push -u <remote> <force-opts...> --progress <all ref names...> [--no-verify] --atomic`
   where `<force-opts>` is per-branch `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<name>:<remoteSha>` (bare `--force-with-lease` when no sha is recorded). `--atomic` is always present on this path. N single-ref pushes each carrying `--atomic` cover one ref apiece and are therefore not atomic across the stack.
5. THEN sequential single-entry submit POSTs, one per branch, bottom-up.
6. A failure mid-loop throws: remaining branches are NOT submitted, all refs are already pushed, earlier PRs stay created. There is no rollback. A refusal must therefore name the PRs that landed and say the branches are pushed.

## The zod request schema (graphite-cli 1.7.20)

Top level: `repoOwner` (req), `repoName` (req), `trunkBranchName` (req), `targetTrunkBranchName?`, `mergeWhenReady?`, `rerequestReview?`, `comment?`, `gti?`, `useWebSubmit?`, `prs` (req, array of create|update union), `webSubmitAnalytics?`.

create entry: `action:"create"`, `head`, `headSha`, `base`, `baseSha`, `title` — all required; `body?`, `draft?`, `reviewers?`, `shouldRetarget?`.
update entry: `action:"update"`, `head`, `headSha`, `base`, `baseSha`, `prNumber` — all required; `title?`, `body?`, `draft?`, `reviewers?`, `rebaseOnlyChange?`, `maintainRetarget?`.

No cross-entry refinements, no ordering rule, no max length. The published transport schema permits the array; the server-side handler is stricter than the contract it publishes. That is why 0.52.0 believed batching was safe.

## Two real gt POST bodies (golden-test material)

```json
{"prs":[{"head":"parent","headSha":"fc044e738a85ae934a69924b52bd77c0968149ff","base":"main","baseSha":"a4a11847106d0378d4f339fe87a84287bc2c4633","action":"create","title":"parent","body":"","draft":true,"shouldRetarget":false,"reviewers":[]}],"trunkBranchName":"main"}
{"prs":[{"head":"child","headSha":"62953f200e94a57402e235cc6b4d3339045312c7","base":"parent","baseSha":"fc044e738a85ae934a69924b52bd77c0968149ff","action":"create","title":"child","body":"","draft":true,"shouldRetarget":false,"reviewers":[]}],"trunkBranchName":"main"}
```

## Do not

- Re-batch `prs`. One entry per POST, looped in stack order.
- Add `shouldRetarget:false` / `reviewers:[]` to mirror gt's bodies: ccx omits both and its single-entry submit succeeded, so they are proven harmless.
- Move `pre-submit-pull-requests` into the loop, or start consuming `retargetedPrs`. gt calls it once and ignores the result.
- Change body/omitempty handling: `body` is optional and gt sends `body:""` successfully.
- Change how `baseSha` is derived. See the sibling note "baseSha is gt's recorded parent_branch_revision, by reference".

Code: `gtSubmitStack` / `gtSubmitPRs` / `gtPushArgv` in internal/cli/shipgt.go; `SubmitRequest` / `SubmitPR` / `SubmitPullRequests` in internal/gtapi/routes.go.
